title: Alleged coercion of VP Sara's ex-staffer a 'coordinated social media activity' — NBI
summary: The claims of supposed coercion of the former staff of Vice President Sara Duterte are a coordinated social media activity, according to National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag.

blocks.text: November 17, 2026 | 5:07pm
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte (front R) leaves court after posting bail in Quezon City, suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — The claims of supposed coercion of the former staff of Vice President Sara Duterte are a coordinated social media activity, according to National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag.

In a Zoom press conference on November 17, Matibag said that the agency only observed simultaneous postings across social media platforms about the narrative, which points to a coordinated effort to spread the narrative online.
"Wala kaming na-receive except maraming nagpasa nung mga it appears to be coordinated behavior sa social media na sabay-sabay na nag-post na merong ganitong pangyayari," Matibag said.
(We have not received anything, except many people forwarded what appears to be coordinated behavior on social media, simultaneously posting that such an incident happened.)
"Sana there should be a formal report so we can investigate. Kung ayaw sa amin, there is PNP," he added.
(Hopefully, there will be a formal report so we can investigate. If they don't want to file it with us, there is the PNP.)
Matibag added that the bureau has received zero formal complaints or referrals regarding the alleged incident.
Earlier, in a message to Philstar.com, Matibag said that if they feel the urgency to report the incident, Duterte's camp should file a complaint.
Without any clear documentation or concrete evidence, the NBI chief dismissed the online allegations as mere rumors.
"Well, overall reaction eh pagka wala tayong malinaw na document of evidence, I will borrow the words nila na ginagamit ay chismis lang yan," Matibag said.
(Well, as an overall reaction, if we do not have a clear document of evidence, I will borrow the words they use—that is just gossip.)

The first Facebook post came in the morning on Tuesday from former human rights lawyer and presidential spokesperson Harry Roque, who claimed that the vice president received a message from what appeared to be the account of a former household staff member containing a "desperate plea for help and rescue in Manila."

He added that the sender claimed to be under the custody or control of certain individuals who allegedly warned of a threat to the former staffer's life and tried to force them to sign a document, which they refused to execute.

Also in his post, Roque likened the alleged incident to that of Jefry Tupas, claiming that NBI agents had previously told Tupas on Sept. 29, 2026, of threats to his life before attempting to bring him to Manila.
Hours later, the same Facebook post was copy-pasted by lawyer Paolo Duterte, who is one of the spokespersons of the vice president.

Rep. Paolo Duterte (Davao City 1st District) at 10:38 a.m. then called the actions a tactic to intimidate and pressure individuals into signing documents and acting as witnesses to fabricate a case against his sister.

Aside from the impeachment trial, Duterte is also facing a grave threat charge before a Quezon City Regional Trial Court over her threats in October and November 2024 press conferences against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

The NBI is also investigating alleged irregularities in the properties of the vice president and her husband, Manases Carpio, which are indicated in their Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth.
